steps.notes: wrap = np.mod(r, L) into [0,L); targets confirm; no ambiguity (test inputs incl. negatives disambiguate vs [-L/2,L/2) only via target, but [0,L) is the universal reading of 'within the cubic box').

Passes only with the unstated convention r12 = min-image(r2 - r1). The equally natural r1 - r2 fails all 3 tests (probe verified). Docstring Returns line is a copy-paste of dist ('float: The minimum image distance').
Truncated+shifted LJ; formula given explicitly. r==rc boundary in test 0 is outcome-identical for < vs <= (V(r)=V(rc) => 0). Clean.

Passes only with r read as displacement FROM i TO j (force on i = -24*eps*[2(s/r)^12-(s/r)^6]*r/r^2). Allen-Tildesley textbook reading (r = r_i - r_j) fails tests 1-2 (probe verified). Docstring also wrongly types r as 'float: distance'.
Target = stated background formula DIVIDED by V=L^3; literal implementation of the printed formula is 1000x off and fails (probe verified). Docstring also lists phantom param 'r'.

Target = stated background formula divided by V^2 then converted zJ/nm^3 -> bar (x10); literal formula fails (probe verified). bar conversion itself is inferable from problem-level units; the missing 1/V^2 is not. Phantom param 'r' in docstring.
Pairwise sum of E_ij with min-image dist; no tail correction (targets confirm). Clean (phantom 'r' docstring param only).

Physics fully specified (kB given, unit conversions inferable). BUT test 0 feeds v as shape (3,) while docstring promises (N,3): per-particle implementations using axis=1/norm(axis=1) crash with AxisError and fail officially (probe verified).

Passes only with virial = sum f_ij(r_i->j) . r_i->j, which equals MINUS the physical virial pressure. Standard textbook virial fails test 2 (probe verified: physical P_virial = +8.8505 bar, target = -8.8505 bar). Test 1 also feeds N=2 with a 3-row xyz (harmless for virial, but kinetic term must use the N parameter).

Physically correct force targets. BUT test 1 sets N=2 while xyz has 3 rows; target shape is (2,3) so only the first N rows may be used; vectorized-over-xyz implementations crash on np.allclose broadcast and fail officially (probe verified).

Reasonable implementation passes in 36 s (well under official 1800 s; even mostly pure-Python solutions fit). Target bool = True. Robust to thermostat-as-rescaling vs additional-force and to virial sign (physical-sign pressure variant also passes). NOT robust to the isothermal compressibility gamma, whose value (4.6e-5 1/bar) appears only in hidden test code; and a barostat-less implementation passes.

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'calculates the minimum image vector between two atoms'; docstring gives no direction and its Returns line is a copy-paste error from step 77.2 ('Returns: float: The minimum image distance.' while the function returns a vector r12). h5 targets encode min-image(r2 - r1): test 0 r1=[2,3,4], r2=[2.5,3.5,4.5] -> target [0.5,0.5,0.5] = r2-r1; test 1 target [-2,-2,-2] = min-image(r2-r1). A probe implementing the equally natural r1 - r2 (the Allen-Tildesley r_ij = r_i - r_j convention, arguments in order) FAILS all 3 tests under official joint scoring (review/work/77/probe_alt.py). Pure 50/50 sign guess.
findings.suggested_fix: State the direction in the docstring, e.g. 'Returns: r12: numpy 1d array, the minimum-image displacement vector FROM r1 TO r2 (r2 - r1, wrapped).' Also fix the Returns type ('float'->'array').

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'calculates the forces between two particles whose three dimensional displacement is r'; docstring: 'Returns: array_like: The force vector experienced by particle i due to particle j' and (wrongly) 'r (float): The distance between particles i and j'. The direction of the displacement is never stated. Target test 1 (sigma=2, r=[3,-4,5], rc=10) = [+7.3653e-4, -9.8203e-4, +1.2275e-3] = -24*eps*(2(s/r)^12-(s/r)^6)*r/|r|^2, i.e. r must be read as the displacement FROM i TO j (r_j - r_i). The standard Allen-Tildesley reading (r = r_i - r_j, F_i = +24*eps*[...]*r/r^2) gives the exact negative and FAILS tests 1-2 officially (probe_alt.py). Test 0 (|r|=2.57 > rc=2, zero target) is sign-blind, so the step hinges entirely on this unstated 50/50 convention.
findings.suggested_fix: In the docstring define r explicitly: 'r: 3D displacement vector from particle i to particle j (r_j - r_i)'; fix the 'float distance' type error.

findings.evidence: Background states: 'The energy tail correction per particle is given by: u_i = (8/3) pi N^2 epsilon sigma^3 [ (1/3)(sigma/rc)^9 - (sigma/rc)^3 ]'. This formula (a) is labeled per-particle yet contains N^2 and (b) is missing the 1/V factor of the standard result U_tail = (8 pi N^2 eps sigma^3)/(3V) [...]. The h5 targets equal the printed formula divided by L^3 (test 0: printed formula = -22.3402, target = -0.0223402). A literal implementation of the supplied formula is 1000x off and FAILS all tests officially (probe_alt.py). Only a solver who overrides the printed equation with domain knowledge (cued by the otherwise-unused L parameter and 'for the entire system' in the docstring) passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the background formula to U_tail = (8 pi N^2 epsilon sigma^3)/(3 V) [ (1/3)(sigma/rc)^9 - (sigma/rc)^3 ], V = L^3, and drop the 'per particle' wording (or use N*rho form).

findings.evidence: Background states: 'p_tail = (16/3) pi N^2 epsilon sigma^3 [ (2/3)(sigma/rc)^9 - (sigma/rc)^3 ]' — missing the 1/V^2 of the standard P_tail = (16 pi N^2 eps sigma^3)/(3 V^2)[...]; as printed it is dimensionally an energy, not a pressure. Targets equal printed formula / L^6, converted zJ/nm^3 -> bar (x10): test 0 printed = -22.3402, target = -2.23402e-4 bar. Literal implementation FAILS officially (probe_alt.py); off by 1e6 before the unit conversion. (The zJ/nm^3 -> bar factor of 10 itself is inferable from the problem-level units and is not flagged.)
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the background formula to P_tail = (16 pi N^2 epsilon sigma^3)/(3 V^2) [ (2/3)(sigma/rc)^9 - (sigma/rc)^3 ] and state the zJ/nm^3 -> bar conversion (1 zJ/nm^3 = 10 bar).

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'v_xyz : ndarray A NumPy array with shape (N, 3)'. Test 0 passes v=np.array([1,2,3]) (shape (3,)) with N=1 — out-of-contract input. A natural per-particle implementation (background says 'the kinetic energy for each particle is given by ...') using np.sum(v**2, axis=1) or np.linalg.norm(v, axis=1) crashes: 'numpy.exceptions.AxisError: axis 1 is out of bounds for array of dimension 1' -> official joint FAIL (probe_t9_axis.py; isolated mode confirms only test 0 fails). Only shape-agnostic np.sum(v**2) implementations pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Change test 0 input to v=np.array([[1,2,3]]) (shape (1,3)) — target value is unchanged.

findings.evidence: Target test 2 P_virial = -8.850528286177664 bar, but the configuration (5 particles, pair 0-3 at r=0.7125 < 2^(1/6) sigma, strongly repulsive) has physical virial pressure +8.850528 bar (independent recomputation with the standard W = sum_{i<j} F_on_i . (r_i - r_j)). The frozen target is the exact NEGATIVE of the physical value; total pressure target -8.712 bar is unphysical for a repulsion-dominated state. Cause: background defines 'f_ij is the force on particle i exerted by particle j ... r_ij is the displacement vector from particle i to j' — this i->j/force-on-i pairing flips the sign of the standard virial. A solver writing the standard (correct-physics) virial FAILS test 2 officially (probe_alt.py); passing requires both following the flipped convention here AND having guessed step 77.5's unstated displacement direction the same way (cross-step coupling). Tests 0-1 have zero virial and cannot catch the sign.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate test-2 target with the standard virial (P_virial = +8.8505, total = +8.9886 bar), or redefine the background convention consistently (r_ij = r_i - r_j with f_ij = force on i) so the formula yields the physical sign.

findings.evidence: Test 1 sets N = 2 but passes a 3-row positions array (docstring: 'xyz ... shape (N, 3)'). An implementation deriving the particle count from xyz.shape[0] for the kinetic term gives P_kinetic = 3*kB*T/V*10 instead of target 2.7613e-4 bar (=N=2) and fails test 1 (probe_p10_lenxyz.py, isolated: test 1 AssertionError). Virial happens to be insensitive (all pairs beyond rc=2 whether 2 or 3 particles are used). Mis-score risk is lower than 77.11 because the explicit N parameter is the obvious choice for N*kB*T/V.
findings.suggested_fix: Make test 1 self-consistent: either N=3 with the 3-row array (requires regenerating the target) or drop the third row.

findings.evidence: Test 1 sets N = 2 but passes a 3-row positions array, violating the docstring contract 'xyz : ndarray ... shape (N, 3)' / 'Returns ... shape (N, 3)'. The h5 target has shape (2,3) and contains only the 0-1 pair interaction, so the reference iterated over range(N) and silently ignored row 2. A standard vectorized implementation over all rows of xyz returns shape (3,3) and crashes the assert: 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,3) (2,3)' -> official FAIL (probe_alt.py). Both implementations are correct under the documented contract; only the test input is out of contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Set N=3 in test 1 and regenerate the target (or remove the third row and keep the existing (2,3) target).

findings.evidence: Background gives the barostat as eta(t) = 1 - (dt/tau_P) * gamma * (P_target - P(t)) where 'gamma is the isothermal compressibility' — but no value is supplied anywhere in the prompt/background/docstring, gamma is not a parameter of velocityVerlet, and the value used (gamma = 4.6E-5  # 1/bar, water) exists only inside the hidden test code. The simulated system is argon (m = 39.948 g/mol), so guessing argon's compressibility is at least as defensible: probe with gamma=2e-4 (liquid argon scale) FAILS ('Exception: Berendsen barostat shrank the box below twice the cutoff radius', the exception the docstring itself mandates); gamma=5e-3 (ideal-gas 1/P at 200 bar) FAILS (eta<0 -> NaN -> AssertionError). gamma=4.5e-5 and 4.6e-5 PASS (out_g*.log). The step is solvable only by guessing the authors' canonical-water-compressibility choice.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the step background/docstring: 'use isothermal compressibility gamma = 4.6e-5 bar^-1', or add gamma as a function parameter.

findings.evidence: The single test only asserts (|mean(T_sim - 298)|/298 < 0.3 and |mean(P_sim[240:] - 200)|/200 < 0.3) == True. A deliberately wrong implementation that ignores the barostat entirely (never rescales L or positions; impl_nobarostat.py) PASSES officially (out_nobarostat.log), because the initial density happens to give a mean pressure within the 30 percent band. So the integration step never verifies barostat functionality — while simultaneously failing honest barostat implementations that picked a different compressibility (see D2 finding). The thermostat is exercised, the barostat is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the pressure band (e.g. 10 percent) and/or additionally assert that the box length changed from its initial value (L_final != 2.4) so a no-op barostat cannot pass.

findings.evidence: Docstring (and problem_io) parameter description is garbled: 'P_target : float Target pressure for the Berendsen barostat, units: bar.ostat. Set to 0 to deactivate, units: picoseconds.' — a duplicated/corrupted fragment of the tau_P line; P_target's deactivation semantics and units read nonsensically. Unlikely to flip scores (the bar unit is still legible) but should be cleaned.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'P_target : float — Target pressure for the Berendsen barostat, units: bar.'

overall_assessment: Not fair to score as-is. Although every step is technically passable (verified end-to-end: a target-convention implementation passes all 12 steps, 77.12 in 36 s), 8 of 12 steps carry score-flipping defects: two pure 50/50 sign/direction conventions (77.3, 77.5) that nothing in the text pins down; two background formulas printed without their volume factors (77.6 x1000 off, 77.7 x1e6 off) so the literal prompt is wrong; out-of-contract test inputs that crash contract-faithful implementations (77.9 shape (3,) vs (N,3); 77.11 N=2 with 3-row xyz); a frozen virial-pressure target that is the exact negative of the physical value (77.10); and a final step that both requires guessing a hidden compressibility constant (4.6e-5/bar, present only in test code — plausible alternatives crash or NaN) and fails to detect a missing barostat. A competent, physics-literate solver would realistically lose 4-6 of 12 steps to data defects rather than ability.
